Forklift driver David Yelsa was working when the forklift suddenly malfunctioned and rolled over, crushing him to death. According to the rules, if something goes wrong, you should notify your family, report it to the government, and cooperate with the investigation. But Rongtai wanted to secretly transport the body away. When the local people discovered it, they immediately exploded. What's even more outrageous is that the security guards at the factory opened fire on the gathered crowd, killing another person. The crowd rushed into the factory, smashed, looted and burned. Equipment, vehicles and office areas were all destroyed, and many Chinese employees were injured. Two lives lost: a forklift driver and a civilian shot in the conflict. The deputy governor asked four consecutive questions. Dennis Idahosa, the deputy governor of Edo State, rushed to the scene and inspected the core area of ​​the accident inch by inch. Then he raised four issues: First, the forklift responsible for the accident had been removed in advance - the official investigation team had not yet arrived, and the key evidence was gone. Second, there was no blood at the accident scene. A man was crushed to death by heavy machinery, and the ground was clean. title_en: Nokia China announced that it will lay off about 1,600 employees! Nokia China announced that it will lay off about 1,600 employees and close its core R&D center in Hangzhou. Sites in Beijing, Chengdu and other places will also be adjusted simultaneously. The relevant work is expected to be completed before the end of 2026. This is a key step in Nokia's years of business contraction in China: it has previously missed core domestic 5G orders, accounting for less than 3% of the Chinese 5G market, and its employee base has plummeted from 13,700 in 2020 to 7,200 in 2025. The special investment of 350 million euros in this restructuring is an important part of its global 800 million euro cost reduction plan. After completion, it will save 200 million euros in operating costs every year. This communications giant, which once occupied the youthful memories of Chinese people, is using a drastic reduction method to shift resources to new tracks such as 6G research and development and AI data center infrastructure, in an attempt to regain its position in the global market. #worship[topic]# #employment[topic]# #foreign enterprise[topic]# #Internet major factory[topic]# #future work trend[topic]# # Layoffs[topic]# #科技 Information Early Know[topic]#

title_en: The Philippine Defense Secretary commanded the army to arrest Chinese workers! Eight questions, Teodoro's underwear was stripped clean. On the evening of August 15, Ji Lingpeng, spokesperson of the Chinese Embassy in the Philippines, responded to Philippine Defense Secretary Teodoro’s statement. Eight questions, every sentence is bloody. 🟡 First, who gave you the power to arrest people, as the defense minister did? Teodoro commanded the army to rush to the Sanjia Steel Factory to arrest unarmed Chinese workers. Is he the defense minister or the police chief? Law enforcement is the responsibility of the police, while the military is responsible for fighting. The Minister of Defense personally led a team to arrest the workers - this was not an act of overstepping his authority, but an abuse of power. 🟡Second, selective law enforcement, why only arrest Chinese people? If a factory violates environmental protection laws, why not arrest the boss and the person in charge, but only the workers? Why were only the Chinese workers arrested and the Filipino workers released on the spot? The evidence of selective enforcement is on the table. 🟡Third, it’s a frame-up, a textbook level frame-up. Workers only wear normal work clothes on weekdays. On the day of the raid, law enforcement officers asked three Chinese workers to put on protective clothing and pose for photos, hyping up the hype that "Chinese workers wear protective clothing but Filipino workers do not." This is not law enforcement, this is acting. 🟡 Fourth, 5
